checks.claim: A wing's curved shape, called an airfoil, turns the passing air so the wing is pushed up.
checks.why: Pilot Institute and Smithsonian: the airfoil's shape and angle turn the air down and make lower pressure on top; the reaction pushes the wing up.

sources.title: What Is an Airfoil? How Lift is Generated - Pilot Institute
How does an airfoil lift - Smithsonian How Things Fly

checks.claim: Ailerons roll an airplane, the elevator pitches its nose up and down, and the rudder swings the nose left and right.
checks.why: NASA and Wikipedia: ailerons control roll, elevators pitch, the rudder yaw; the rudder also counters the adverse yaw of a roll.

checks.claim: Many airplanes carry their fuel in tanks inside the wings.
checks.why: Wikipedia: the most common method is integral tanks inside the wings (wet wings).

sources.title: Why Airplanes Store Fuel in the Wings - AeroCorner

checks.claim: Flaps let an airplane fly more slowly for landing.
checks.why: Extending flaps lowers the stall speed, so the plane approaches and touches down slower, with a shorter roll.
